abac.short: Policy evaluated against (subject, resource, action, environment) attributes; expressive but complex.

acid-transaction.short: Atomic, Consistent, Isolated, Durable — guaranteed for single-database operations; the gold standard you're giving up when spanning databases.

alert-fatigue.short: When so many alerts fire that on-call engineers start ignoring all of them, including critical ones.

anti-join.short: A LEFT JOIN kept only where the right side is NULL — the rows with no match. How you find what is missing (a neglected asset), which a query starting from the present side can never see.

api-documentation.short: Describes endpoints, request/response schemas, auth requirements, error codes, and rate limits. OpenAPI/Swagger is the standard format.

append-only.short: Audit records are inserted, never updated or deleted; enforced at the database permission level, not just application logic.

audit-log.short: Every secret read is logged with timestamp, requester identity, and secret name; critical for compliance (SOC 2, GDPR).

aws-secrets-manager.short: Paid; adds automatic rotation for RDS passwords, first-class versioning, and cross-account sharing.

b-tree-index.short: The default PostgreSQL index type; supports =, <, >, BETWEEN, LIKE 'prefix%' efficiently.

backward-compatibility.short: New code can read data written by old code — old records remain readable after a schema change.

base.short: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency — the alternative to ACID for distributed systems; AP systems are BASE systems.

billable-utilization.short: Billable delivery hours ÷ total work hours — used for capacity insight, never as a self-punishment metric.

binary-search.short: O(log n), but only valid on sorted/monotonic data — check the precondition before reaching for it.

blast-radius.short: The scope of impact from a chaos experiment; start small (1 instance, staging environment).

bounded-context.short: An explicit boundary where a term has exactly one model and meaning.

breaking-change.short: Any change that would cause an existing client to break — removing a field, changing a field type, changing required/optional status, changing authentication scheme.

cache-invalidation.short: Deleting or updating cache entries when source data changes — the hardest problem in caching.

change-request-process.short: Every fixed-price package needs an explicit path for "what happens when the client asks for something not in scope" — without this, every such request becomes a negotiation from scratch.

circuit-breaker.short: Tracks recent failure rates for calls to an external dependency and "opens" once failures exceed a threshold, making further calls fail fast instead of piling up on a slow or dead service — then probes with a half-open state before closing again.

code-generation.short: The final stage; walks the (possibly transformed) AST and emits output text (JavaScript, binary, SQL, etc.).

composition-root.short: The one place (app startup) where you wire Ports to Adapters; the only place that imports both.

connection-pooling.short: Maintains a set of pre-established database connections that application instances share, so requests avoid the cost of a fresh TCP handshake, authentication, and session setup every time.

constant-time-comparison.short: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual() to compare HMACs; regular string comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks.

constructor-injection.short: The idiomatic DI pattern: dependencies are passed in as constructor arguments.

consumer-groups.short: A way to have multiple independent "logical consumers" each get their own copy of a topic, while each group internally load-balances across its workers.

content-negotiation.short: Accept: application/vnd.company.v2+json — HTTP-purist approach, rare in practice.

context-propagation.short: The mechanism that carries the active span context into async callbacks, Promise chains, and across HTTP boundaries via AsyncLocalStorage.

correlation-id.short: A unique ID injected into each log line (often the traceId) that lets you find all logs for one request.

cqrs.short: Separates the command model (write) from the query model (read); each is optimized independently.

criticality.short: How much an asset's failure matters — consequence times likelihood against the organisation's own tolerance. A property of the role, roughly constant over life; not condition, and never a vendor number.

crosswalk.short: A table holding one row per (canonical asset, source system, external id), each time-bounded, so an id in one system can be resolved to the same asset's id in another as of a given moment.

cve.short: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures; a numbered, publicly documented security vulnerability in a specific software version.

dangling-edge.short: An edge in a network graph whose from- or to-node is not in the node table — usually a node deleted from one table and not the other. Invisible on a map, and it breaks any traversal passing through it.

data-minimization.short: Collect only the PII necessary for the stated purpose; less data collected = less data to delete.

data-residency.short: Some data classes (health, biometric, government-classified) carry a legal requirement to stay within a specific country's borders, independent of which cloud provider is used.

data-retention-policy.short: Automatically drop partitions/chunks older than a threshold; more efficient than DELETE WHERE created_at < $threshold.

database-sharding.short: Horizontally partitions data across multiple independent database instances, each holding only a subset of the total data — unlike replication, where every node holds all of it. The shard key (the field that decides which shard a row lands on) is the critical design choice.

dead-tuples.short: Old row versions left behind by UPDATE/DELETE. They occupy space until vacuumed.

dependency-rule.short: Dependencies only point inward; the core never imports adapters.

dip.short: High-level modules should not import low-level modules directly; both should depend on an abstraction (interface).

dkim.short: Two keys — private key held by your email provider signs each outgoing message; public key in DNS is used by receivers to verify the signature; each selector can be different per provider.

dmarc.short: DNS TXT record specifying policy (p=none, p=quarantine, p=reject) and reporting email; start with p=none to observe before enforcing.

domain-event.short: Something meaningful that happened in the domain (OrderShipped), decoupled from how other parts react to it (ties to #131 Message Queues, #14 Outbox Pattern).

domain-sharding.short: HTTP/1.1 trick of spreading assets across multiple domains to win more parallel connections — counterproductive under HTTP/2, where it defeats connection reuse and header compression.

eager-loading.short: Pre-fetching related data in the initial query (via JOIN or a second bulk query) — Prisma's include.

effective-hourly-rate.short: Total revenue ÷ total hours worked (including admin, sales, unpaid revisions). This is usually much lower than your stated rate.

error-budget.short: (1 - SLO_target) × window; the amount of failures you can afford before breaching.

event-store.short: An append-only log of events, keyed by aggregate ID and ordered by sequence number.

event-stream.short: All events for a single aggregate, identified by an aggregateId.

eventual-consistency.short: Accepts that different parts of a distributed system may be briefly out of sync, and designs the system to converge to a consistent state over time — a deliberate trade of synchronous consistency for availability and performance, not "eventual incorrectness."

exponential-backoff.short: Spreads out retries after a failed operation instead of retrying immediately, so a recovering service doesn't get hit by every client at once. Usually paired with jitter, which randomizes the delay so retries from many clients don't all land on the same second.

feature-flag.short: A runtime switch that controls whether a feature is visible inside an already-deployed version of the code, decoupling deployment from release — code can ship dark, then be turned on for a small percentage of users before everyone.

flame-graph.short: Visualization of CPU time per function. Width = time spent. Read top-down for hot paths.

functional-location.short: An identifier for a position in the plant — "the booster pump on set 01" — as opposed to the serial number, which identifies the unit currently installed there. The register keys on this; a replacement changes the serial and not the location.

git-bisect.short: Binary search over commit history to isolate a regression.

global-id.short: IFC's own identifier: a 128-bit UUID compressed into 22 characters. Unique within a file by schema rule; stable across exports only if the exporter chooses to keep it.

graceful-degradation.short: The system continues serving reduced functionality when a dependency fails; the opposite of hard dependencies everywhere.

hard-bounce.short: Email address does not exist — permanently undeliverable; must be suppressed immediately and never retried.

hashicorp-vault.short: Self-hosted or cloud; most feature-rich; dynamic secrets (generates a new DB credential per request); heavy operational overhead.

heap-snapshot.short: A dump of all live objects in V8's heap at a moment in time. Comparing two snapshots shows what was allocated and not collected.

hmac.short: Hash-based Message Authentication Code. Proves both integrity and authenticity — the sender has the secret key. This is what JWT HS256 uses.

hmac-sha256.short: Hash-based Message Authentication Code using SHA-256; proves the payload was generated by the secret holder and hasn't been tampered with.

idempotency-key.short: A unique identifier per logical operation (Stripe uses Idempotency-Key header; your own operations need equivalent protection) — guarantees at-most-once or exactly-once semantics.

ifc.short: Industry Foundation Classes — an EXPRESS schema plus a serialization (usually the STEP Physical File) for exchanging building models between tools.

index-bloat.short: Over time, dead tuples accumulate in indexes; VACUUM reclaims them; REINDEX CONCURRENTLY rebuilds without locking.

index-only-scan.short: Uses a covering index; no heap fetch needed; fastest for covered queries.

integration-contract.short: A short per-source document stating what data the integration will receive, in what identity, clock, units and cadence, with what quality and change guarantees, and what happens when the source goes silent. Written before the sensors are installed.

integration-test.short: Tests a real component against real infrastructure (test DB, test Redis); slower but higher confidence.

kill-switch.short: A flag whose only purpose is to disable a feature in production without a deploy.

kvkk.short: Turkish equivalent of GDPR; applies to any service processing data of Turkish citizens; same practical requirements as GDPR for most operational purposes.

lamport-clock.short: A per-node counter, bumped on each local event and set to max(local, received)+1 on receiving a message. Guarantees that if A caused B then lamport(A) < lamport(B) — a causal order that needs no synchronised clock.

lazy-loading.short: Fetching related data only when accessed — triggers per-item queries; often the root cause of N+1.

lockfile-integrity.short: Package-lock.json pins exact versions and hashes; CI should run npm ci (not npm install) to enforce the lockfile.

mass-assignment.short: Binding a user-supplied object directly to a database entity without field filtering.

materialized-view.short: A stored query result in PostgreSQL; refreshed explicitly; faster reads at the cost of data freshness.

modular-monolith.short: One deployable, enforced internal module boundaries — often the right first step.

mrr.short: Monthly Recurring Revenue — sum of all active subscriptions normalized to monthly; the most fundamental SaaS metric.

n-plus-1-query.short: 1 query to fetch a list, N queries to fetch related data per item — total N+1 round trips.

nested-loop.short: For each row in the outer set, scan the inner set; fast when inner set is small and indexed; slow when outer set is large.

outbox-relay.short: A process that reads unpublished outbox entries and publishes them to the message broker.

partial-index.short: Index with a WHERE clause; indexes only matching rows; smaller and faster to maintain than a full index.

password-hashing.short: One-way, salted, deliberately slow (bcrypt/argon2) — never plain SHA-256, never reversible encryption.

pool-exhaustion.short: When all connections are in use and a new request can't get one; results in timeout or 500 error.

primary-key.short: Uniquely identifies a row in a table; a foreign key in another table references it, enforcing referential integrity.

principle-of-least-privilege.short: Assign the minimum role required; avoid creating "super roles" that span multiple unrelated permissions.

productized-service.short: Fixed scope + fixed price + documented delivery process. Repeatable.

prompt-injection.short: Untrusted retrieved or user-supplied content containing instructions that hijack the model's behavior — treat any injected text as untrusted input, same posture as #29 OWASP.

property-set.short: The open-ended bag IFC keeps discipline data in, attached to an element by a relationship instead of being a field on it. Published ones carry a Pset_ prefix.

race-condition.short: Two concurrent transactions both read the same state and both proceed to write, producing an inconsistent final state.

rag-pipeline.short: Embed documents → store in a vector DB → embed the query → retrieve top-k similar chunks → inject into the prompt.

rate-limiting.short: Controls how many requests a client can make in a given period. Token bucket, leaky bucket, and sliding window are the common algorithms, and they trade off burst tolerance, fairness, and implementation cost differently — one algorithm for every endpoint is almost always the wrong choice.

rbac.short: Permissions assigned to roles; users assigned to roles; simple, auditable, correct for 80% of SaaS use cases.

read-replica.short: A continuously synchronized copy of a database that accepts only read (SELECT) queries. Writes go to the primary and stream to replicas asynchronously, with some replication lag before they're visible there.

readiness-probe.short: Kubernetes health check that gates traffic to a new pod; only routes traffic once the pod is healthy.

replication-lag.short: The delay between a write on the primary and its visibility on the replica; can be milliseconds to seconds.

residual-risk.short: The risk that remains after controls are applied — must be named explicitly in the register, never left implied by silence.

retained-size.short: Memory a node keeps alive (itself + everything reachable only through it). Leak investigation starts here.

retention-policy.short: Compliance standards (GDPR, PCI-DSS) specify minimum and maximum retention periods; implement automated archival.

retry-policy.short: Exponential backoff with a cap (e.g., 1s, 5s, 30s, 5m, 30m, 2h, 12h, 24h); total max attempts ~8–10.

risk-register.short: A living table (Risk / Level / Impact / Control / Owner / Residual Risk) revisited whenever scope changes, not a document written once at kickoff.

rolling-update.short: Replacing a fraction of instances at a time; used by Kubernetes Deployments by default.

root-span.short: The first span in a trace; created by the service that receives the original request.

scope-definition.short: Which URLs, APIs, and features are in-scope; what attack types are permitted (no DDoS, no social engineering of employees); defines what the tester can legally do.

scoped-packages.short: @yourusername/package-name — scoped packages prevent name collisions and signal authorship; required for GitHub Packages, optional but recommended for npm.

secrets-manager.short: A dedicated service for storing, rotating, and auditing access to credentials (API keys, DB passwords, JWT secrets).

seq-scan.short: Full table scan; acceptable for small tables or low-selectivity filters; bad for large tables with selective filters.

shallow-size.short: Memory the object itself uses, not counting references. Usually small.

shared-schema.short: Weakest isolation; all tenants in shared tables with tenantId discriminator; simplest to build, highest risk of data leakage.

singleton-scope.short: The container creates one instance and caches it; subsequent requests return the same object.

sla.short: A contractual SLO with consequences (credits, exits); always weaker than your internal SLO.

sli.short: A specific measurable indicator: successful_requests / total_requests, p99_latency_ms, checkout_completion_rate.

slo.short: A target threshold for an SLI over a time window: "99.5% availability over 30 days".

soft-delete.short: DeletedAt TIMESTAMP NULL column; NULL = active, non-null = deleted; queries filter on WHERE deletedAt IS NULL.

spatial-containment.short: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure: places a physical element into exactly one spatial structure element, normally a storey. The relationship a viewer tree and a per-storey take-off both read.

sticky-sessions.short: WebSocket connections are stateful — without them, a load balancer may route the same client to a different server on reconnect, losing room membership. Solve with Redis Pub/Sub as a shared message bus.

streaming-replication.short: PostgreSQL's built-in replication mechanism; replicas connect to the primary and receive WAL in real-time.

stress-test.short: Traffic ramped past expected levels to find the breaking point and failure mode.

suspense-boundary.short: A <Suspense fallback={...}> wrapper that tells React "this subtree can be deferred; show the fallback until it resolves".

table-partitioning.short: A single logical table split into multiple physical storage units based on a partition key; queries that filter on the partition key only scan relevant partitions.

tax-reserve.short: Setting aside 20–30% of every payment immediately for tax obligations. Not doing this is the most common freelancer financial mistake.

tcp-handshake.short: SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK sets up a connection before any application data flows — a real, measurable cost per new connection.

tenant-provisioning.short: Creating a new database, running migrations, seeding initial data — should be automated and idempotent.

test-double.short: Umbrella term for mocks, stubs, fakes, and spies.

thundering-herd.short: Many concurrent requests all miss the cache at the same time and flood the DB; prevent with staggered TTLs, lock-based population, or probabilistic early expiration.

timeline-reconstruction.short: Precise chronological sequence of events (detection, diagnosis, mitigation, resolution) — the foundation everything else is built on.

token-bucket.short: Bucket refills at a fixed rate; allows bursts up to bucket capacity; most user-friendly for API limits.

traffic-cutover.short: The moment you flip the load balancer or DNS from old to new; in blue-green this is atomic.

trust-boundary.short: The point where data crosses from a domain you control into one you don't — frontend/backend, backend/third-party API, tenant/tenant.

unit-test.short: Tests one function; all external dependencies are mocked; fast, cheap, high volume.

url-versioning.short: /api/v1/, /api/v2/ — visible, easy to route, most common for REST APIs.

vacuum-freeze.short: Prevents transaction ID wraparound — a critical maintenance operation on long-running databases.

value-based-pricing.short: Price is set by the value delivered to the client, not your cost. A €3000/month SaaS replacing a €50K/year manual process is worth more than 80 hours × €50.

value-object.short: No identity, defined entirely by its attributes, typically immutable.

webhook-signature-verification.short: Every incoming webhook should have its signature verified against your provider's secret before any processing; skipping this allows attackers to forge payment events.

websocket-handshake.short: Starts as HTTP Upgrade request (101 Switching Protocols), then becomes raw TCP frame exchange — no HTTP overhead per message.

whole-life-cost.short: The repair-vs-replace comparison done on cost per year of service each option buys — repair over the years it adds, capital over the new unit's life — rather than one quote against another.

work-order.short: One record of one maintenance intervention: which asset, planned or corrective, raised and completed dates. Accumulated, the work-order table is the maintenance history the anti-join reads.

x-forwarded-for.short: The original client IP, added by each proxy hop — must only be trusted from a known, trusted proxy, never taken as-is from the raw request.

yagni.short: "You Aren't Gonna Need It"; the single most useful design principle for knowing when NOT to apply a pattern.
